svg.title: The ray bench plan: P1, P2 and P9
svg.desc: Top: the 4 KB height grid and a ray walking its cells toward the sun, with the cost model C_ray = C_setup + n C_step. Below, three panels: P1 cycles a ray against n with the predicted band and no measurements yet; P2 the same slice batched, interleaved with the vertex transform, and with the grid in OC-RAM; P9 the movers proxies against one slice. Foot: what each result feeds. Not built.

What the bench feeds, once it has numbers
P1 gives C_ray, which sets the slice k for a 2 ms budget (§5.9) and so the refresh period P = N / (k f) of §5.5.
P2 decides the frame's order: the slice in one batch before the transform (§5.10 step 2), or the grid in OC-RAM.
P9 decides whether the movers' proxies fit beside the slice, or need their own budget.
P3 (the shadow's lag at x60) waits on P1's rate. Every cycle count in §5 stays an ESTIMATE until P1, P2 and P9 replace it.
Bench rules: one console image, both clocks, the cache state stated per run, the grid placed off a 16 KB multiple (see cache-placing-trap).
